# LESSON CAVE -- every station, bearing, distance and coordinate in this fixture is INVENTED.

There is no real "Lesson Cave"; the name, the shots, and the location are made up for teaching. Nothing here came from anybody's survey.

Generated by `tools/make_lesson_cave.js`:

```
CaveCAD -no-dock-icon -no-gui -allow-multiple-instances \
    -autostart tools/make_lesson_cave.js "$PWD"
```

Regenerating is deterministic -- every leg, closing leg and splay is a literal number in the generator, not a seeded random walk, so the file comes back byte-identical every time. The generator also self-checks its own design (one loop resolved, exactly one open end, no ERROR-severity finding, under 40 stations) before writing anything, and refuses to print its success token if any of that fails.

## What this cave is for

Task 9 of the teachable-consolidation plan: a cave small enough to survey in one sitting and rich enough to need every stage of the consolidated six-stage Cave Survey menu -- Start Here, Survey Data, Draw the Map, Put a Reference Under the Map, Finish the Sheet, and Fix and Share. Task 10 (a written curriculum) and Task 11 (an in-app guided first run) are built on top of it.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `LessonCave.dat` | the survey, written by the Compass writer through the format registry |
| `LessonCave_MANIFEST.md` | this file |

`tools/make_lesson_cave.js` also writes a drawing -- `LESSON CAVE.dxf`, built through `CsDraw.survey` exactly as `tools/make_demo_caves.js` builds its own shelf -- into a cave folder at `~/Documents/Cave/lesson/LESSON CAVE/` (or the target folder given on the command line). That drawing is not a repo fixture and is not checked into `testdata/`; it exists so the cave shelf and the guided first run (Task 11) have something real to open.

## Where it is

The entrance (`A1`) sits at the same plausible-but-arbitrary point in the southern Indiana karst that `tools/make_demo_caves.js` uses for its whole shelf -- **38.42137, -86.51884** (WGS84) -- reused deliberately so this project has one fictional point for its generated fixtures, not several. It is not a cave and corresponds to no known entrance. Entrance elevation is 771.30 ft: invented, upland-plausible for that county, and deliberately not zero (see the suite's own elevation-datum trap).

## Shape of the cave

Four trips, 15 stations, one loop, one open end, one wide room:

| Trip | Date | Team | Stations | What it teaches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Entrance series | 2026-03-07 | SCHONEGG, WELLER | A1-A6 | a student's first Notebook page: short (5 legs), every station LRUD'd, gentle grade, nothing surprising |
| Side lead | 2026-03-14 | WELLER, POOLE | B1-B4 | ties into A3 (a trip 1 station) and stops open at B4, so the shelf has a real lead to show as "stopped at" |
| The loop | 2026-03-21 | SCHONEGG, POOLE, HARMON | C1-C2 | leaves A6 (trip 1's far end), wanders through C1-C2, and closes back onto B2 (a trip 2 station) -- a real loop the student watches Survey Stats report on |
| The big room | 2026-03-28 | DUVAL, WELLER, HARMON | D1-D3 | branches off A2 (a trip 1 station) into a wide room walked as its own small perimeter loop (D1-D2-D3-D1), so it ties itself shut instead of leaving a second open end. Wide LRUD and splays scattered off every room station: worth a Cross Section, worth Scatter Breakdown |

Total surveyed length 629.8 ft, plan length 628.7 ft, depth 12.0 ft (measured on the last regeneration; see the block below).

## The loop, and its misclosure

The teaching loop is **A3-A4-A5-A6-C1-C2-B2-B1-A3**. Its closing leg (`C2` -> `B2`) is computed from the two branches' walked positions -- exact geometry, not a guess -- and then taped 0.8% long and swung 1.3 degrees off, which is what gives it a small, real, nonzero misclosure instead of an impossible perfect zero:

**closes 2.60 ft over 333.0 ft = 0.78%** -- under `CsValidate.CLOSURE_WARN_PERCENT` (2%), so Survey Stats reports a clean close with nothing to warn about. The student surveys the loop, closes it, and sees a real number.

The big room's own perimeter (`D1-D2-D3-D1`) closes as a small second loop, an unavoidable side effect of tying the room shut rather than leaving it open -- **0.73 ft over 152.8 ft = 0.48%**, also clean. It is not the designated teaching loop; it exists because a room walked all the way around its own walls is exactly how a real party would survey it.

## The open end

**B4** (trip 2, "Side lead") is the cave's only open end: degree 1, with LRUD recorded (the party measured before turning back), and a note in the file ("stopped -- passage continues, low and wet"). Every other passage either continues, loops back, or is the fixed entrance (`A1`, excluded from open-end detection by convention, same as every other cave in this project).

## The big room

`D1`-`D2`-`D3` is the wide passage: LRUD readings of 13-22 ft on every side (against 2-8 ft everywhere else in the cave), plus seven splay shots scattered across ceiling, walls, and floor for breakdown and a ceiling dome -- worth taking a Cross Section in, and worth running Scatter Breakdown across.
